decisionQuestion: For MIHVER's Shadow Council reviewer packet only (advisory evidence, zero effect on quorum): should the reviewer prompt's rationale generation guidance state both a target character count and a strictly lower hard-ceiling-safe generation budget (e.g. target ~500, generation budget ~600, hard acceptance ceiling 1200 unchanged), or should it state only a single number equal to the acceptance ceiling? Consider: (a) headroom against normal model verbosity variance so first-call compliance is more likely; (b) risk that a two-number scheme confuses a reviewer model into truncating mid-sentence; (c) whether a single number close to the ceiling caused the V3/V4 seat-anthropic CHARACTER_LIMIT failures; (d) provider-neutrality across seat-anthropic, seat-openai, seat-google receiving the identical instruction; (e) whether this is better fixed with a generation-budget instruction alone or would need CLI-level structured-output constraints too, and the trade-off of adding those given truncation risk on constrained token budgets.
evidence: V3 and V4 real Shadow Council exercises both failed ASSESSMENT_VALIDATION because seat-anthropic's rationale exceeded the 1200-character hard acceptance ceiling on the first (and only, non-retried) call.
The hard acceptance ceiling (1200 characters / 4096 UTF-8 bytes) is enforced independently in the parser/builder and is out of scope for this decision -- it must not change.
This vote is advisory evidence only: it has zero effect on ADR-0005 quorum semantics, DecisionRecord.recordHash, or any authorization/execution boundary.
